$comment: Read from the SIA chart set AD 2 LFNR (AIP France, chart dated 2021-12-30): the reporting points come from the coordinates table of the chart,
the notes from the English column of its text pages, both read by a script and checked (each point lies within 80 NM of the aerodrome).
Only what the chart prints is recorded; nothing is deduced. Services, frequencies, elevation, position, magnetic variation and runways
were first extracted automatically from the chart text. Drawings (circuit, routes, radials) are not read.
The charts themselves are (c) SIA and are not redistributed. Flight simulation only: never use for real navigation.

A "fr" object holds the French column of the same chart, copied as printed and never translated: a French note sits at the index of its English twin and is left empty when the twin could not be paired with certainty; the French of the procedures and of the points' purposes is not recorded.
name: Berre - La Fare

source.extraction: chart text, table and English column read by script, checked
source.frenchExtraction: French column of the chart text, read by script and paired with the English sentences

preferredQfuReason: preferred QFU 338, due to prevailing winds, lighting conditions and high terrain
notes: ATS: NIL. The chart header prints these units to call, which are not services of this aerodrome (its air-air frequency apart): .
AD reserved for home based ACFT.
AD available for «Airbus Helicopters» helicopters.
AD available for ULM: only class 3 and 6 ULM, with radio equipment and transponder, are authorized.
Knowledge of the protocols provisions (not published) between Salon, Marseille Provence and Berre-la-Fare is essential to use the AD.
For this reason, the use of the AD by non-based users is subject to the authorisation of DSAC/SE (see AD 1.1) and of the AD operator.
PPR via www.auablf.info HEL routes: see MARSEILLE PROVENCE.
Preferred QFU: 338° due to prevailing winds, lighting conditions and high terrain.

Low altitude patterns and engine failure exercises prohibited on QFU 263° and 083°, due to AEM (NR 9885) (1)TODA RWY 08, 26, 16 and 34 reduced due to obstacles (road, fence,.) in the vicinity of RWYs physical ends.
Due to obstructions in the funnel, takeoffs shall compulsorily start from the opposite end.
Departures Climb above published circuits altitude, not above 900 ft AMSL north of RWY 08-26.
Contact PROVENCE Tower (southbound) or SALON Approach (northbound) before leaving R88.
Arrivals Plan overhead join at 1300 ft AMSL, not above 900 ft AMSL North of RWY 08-26.
AEM on AD (NR 9885): 1100 ft AMSL (1000 ft ASFC) SR-SS.
AD réservé aux ACFT basés.
AD utilisable par les hélicoptères d'«Airbus Helicopters».
AD utilisable par ULM : seuls les ULM de classe 3 et 6, équipés de radio et de transpondeur, sont autorisés.
La connaissance des dispositions prévues par protocoles (non publiés) entre Salon, Marseille Provence et Berre-la-Fare est indispensable pour utiliser l'AD.
A ce titre, l'utilisation du terrain par des usagers nonbasés est soumise à l'autorisation de DSAC/SE (voir AD 1.1) et de l'exploitant d'AD.
PPR via www.auablf.info Cheminements hélicoptères : voir MARSEILLE PROVENCE.
QFU préférentiel : 338° cause vents dominants, conditions d'éclairement et relief.

Tours de piste basse hauteur et exercices de panne interdits en QFU 263° et 083°, cause AEM (N°9885). (1)TODA pistes 08, 26, 16 et 34 réduites cause présence d'obstacles (route, clôture, .) à proximité des extrémités physiques des pistes.
Les décollages, cause obstacles dans la trouée, doivent débuter impérativement à partir de l'extrémité opposée.
Départs Monter au-dessus des circuits de piste publiés, sans dépasser 900 ft AMSL au nord de la piste 08-26.
Contacter PROVENCE Tour (départ vers le sud) ou SALON Approche (départ vers le nord) avant de quitter la R88.
Arrivées Prévoir la verticale AD à 1300 ft AMSL, ne pas dépasser 900 ft AMSL au Nord de la piste 08-26.
AEM sur AD (N° 9885) : 1100 ft AMSL (1000 ft ASFC) SR-SS.
